correctness.rationale: Any finite lawful extension embeds over G: embed by universality and move the copy of G to the named parameter set using homogeneity. Identical labeled extensions yield an automorphism over G and differing diagrams already differ on an atomic formula. Every consistent diagram of a pair over finite G is realized this way. A K_4 using just one new vertex is excluded exactly by triangle-freeness of its parameter neighborhood. A K_4 using both is possible only when xy is an edge, in which case it is excluded exactly by independence of the common neighborhood. These give F² and Q with no multiplicity for permuting named parameters or identifying x with y. For bipartite G, triangle-freeness is automatic and choosing the independent common neighborhood leaves three states per remaining vertex, so the count is 4^n+3^n I_G(1/3); for one vertex all 2^n neighborhoods are allowed. Membership in #P uses unique bit guesses for the labeled diagrams. The bipartition-preserving t-clone construction permits nonempty subsets of clones exactly at the vertices of an independent set, giving I_B((1+z)^t−1). For t=1,…,n+1 the distinct nodes (4/3)^t−1 recover degree-at-most-n I_B by rational interpolation. Nodes, oracle answers for graphs of order at most n(n+1), and the products in Lagrange interpolation have polynomial bit length. The empty graph gives two pair types, one one-type, and requires no hardness query in the reduction. The derived homomorphism reduction in the originality check also independently establishes exact hardness.
residual_risks: The checked reduction is exact and polynomial-time Turing only; it makes no approximate-hardness claim. Recorded finite checks are corroboration, not universal evidence.

evidence: Let J' be the unlooped bipartite graph with four vertices on each side and all cross edges except the exceptional-state pair. It is connected and not complete bipartite, so Dyer–Greenhill makes exact hom(·,J') #P-complete. Nonbipartite inputs have zero homomorphisms. For bipartite G, fixing one of the two orientations of each component's bipartition gives a bijection with hom(G,J); summing orientations gives hom(G,J')=2^(c(G))hom(G,J), including isolated vertices.

The stronger general homomorphism theorem therefore covers the hardness of the weighted graph problem under precisely the bipartite restriction; the reviewed Henson sources do not give the H_4 type-to-coloring bridge on that class.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: After the new interpretation, hardness follows from existing results and the clone proof is an elementary alternative. The distinct content is the exact H_4 joint count and its identification with that established hard graph invariant, not a new generic hardness theorem.

originality.rationale: The fixed-activity partition-function hardness is already implied by a graph-homomorphism dichotomy, and the unary count follows from the previously indexed one-type formula. The supported distinct claim is identifying exactly which diagrams contribute in the K_4-free ambient graph and interpreting that weighted partition function as the adjacent ordered pair-type count on all bipartite parameters, hence locating the arity jump on this restriction. The closest previously indexed higher-arity formula uses H_3, not H_4; indexed H_4 biclique counts match an exact specialization, not arbitrary bipartite or general K_4-free bases. No novelty is credited for the general extension machinery or underlying graph counting hardness.
residual_risks: A bounded comparison does not exclude another publication stating the same H_4 interpretation. Underlying scalar exact counting is demonstrably covered, not just a possible overlap.

value.rationale: With the ambient graph and class of parameter sets held fixed, one extra free variable changes an order-only count into a weighted independent-set invariant. The edge/nonedge split explains precisely where parameter-edge information enters and makes graph-counting tools available for Henson type enumeration. The value is this precise interpretation and boundary in arity, not reproving general #P-hardness for an existing partition function.
residual_risks: Exact counts here do not classify approximate counting, algebraic tuple assignments, or tuples of larger arity.
